A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MaxSup and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Inspection of all 19 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2 supports comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, segmentation, transfer-learning and feature-analysis results, including experimental ablations in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and reports additional transfer, fine-grained classification, calibration, scheduling and runtime results.

M1.justification: The MaxSup objective, top-1-logit penalty, gradients and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Additional alpha schedules are evaluated as experimental variants without replacing the proposed training procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds fine-grained classification on CUB-200 and Stanford Cars and extends linear-transfer evaluation to CIFAR-100, CUB, Flowers, Foods and Pets. This substantially broadens the evaluated data beyond the retained ImageNet, CIFAR and ADE20K experiments.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds evaluated Confidence Penalty and Adaptive Label Smoothing baselines for ImageNet ResNet-50; Confidence Penalty was only discussed in v1. The expanded transfer comparison includes OLS, and the revised logit-density figure adds LS. Existing benchmark comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce ECE evaluation, runtime measurement and further ResNet-50 alpha schedules. Extended linear transfer uses 45 logarithmically spaced regularization values from 10^-6 to 10^5, explicitly wider than Table 3's search. Its higher CIFAR-10 scores therefore represent a different protocol. Existing training and segmentation protocols are retained.

E4.justification: Appendices K–M add calibration analysis, a four-schedule ResNet-50 ablation and computational-efficiency analysis. The logit-distribution comparison also gains an LS curve. Earlier component ablations, training-recipe tests, scheduler comparison and feature projections are retained, including material moved from Appendix G to J.

E5.justification: v2's checklist newly identifies multiple runs and initialization/training-seed variability as the basis of reported mean and standard deviation values. Neither version specifies run counts or individual seeds. Existing uncertainty values remain unchanged, and no increase in runs or new statistical test is established.

E6.justification: New Tables 9–11 and 13–15 add substantial results, including MaxSup accuracies of 82.53% on CUB and 92.25% on Cars, and CIFAR-100 ECE of 2.6% versus LS's 3.8%. Transfer findings are mixed: CE leads on five of six datasets, and OLS exceeds MaxSup on CUB. Original Tables 1–8 remain numerically unchanged apart from rounding; v1 Table 9 becomes v2 Table 12.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, LS decompositions, MaxSup gradients and proofs in Appendices A–C are retained, including the CutMix/Mixup derivation. Appendix M explains standard operation costs but adds no substantive derivation, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that LS amplifies misclassification errors and that penalizing the highest logit preserves feature diversity and improves classification and transfer. v2 separates the empirical contribution into another bullet and highlights accuracy ranges, while retaining the central claims and novelty.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations concerning schedule robustness, negligible computational overhead and advantages over Confidence Penalty and Adaptive LS. It removes v1's unsupported assertion of greater label-noise robustness. The stated open questions about distillation, convergence and low-rank representations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the expanded transfer regularization grid, Confidence Penalty coefficient and Adaptive LS teacher-checkpoint selection, and reports epoch timings. Its code-access pointer changes from GitHub to an anonymous repository. Some existing detail, including the explicit CIFAR-100 Nesterov-momentum setting, is omitted; new fine-grained and calibration setups remain sparsely documented.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for calibration, Adaptive Label Smoothing, CUB and Stanford Cars, with a limited comparison against adaptive smoothing in Appendix H. The main positioning relative to LS, neural collapse, distillation and logit regularization remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Much of the main prose is rewritten. Feature analysis is incorporated into the experiments section, quantitative CAM discussion is merged into the visualization subsection, and limitations and impact are shortened. v2 also adds a NeurIPS checklist, reorganizes the appendices, changes terminology toward error amplification and adds an author.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main paper from two columns to one, extensively resizes and repositions tables, and substantially shrinks the Grad-CAM panel. It adds six tables and redraws the logit-density plot with LS before relocating it to Appendix N. Existing feature projections and the detailed feature-metrics table are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added baselines, broader transfer evaluation, calibration scores and timing measurements provide useful checks of the existing claims. The gain is limited by sparse protocols for new fine-grained and calibration experiments and broad superiority language despite mixed transfer rankings in Table 9. These additions modestly strengthen the paper while leaving its core method, proofs and original benchmark evidence unchanged.
